lead: Detroit has some of the oldest homes in the country and an older combined sewer system. Basement flooding in big storms is the city's most common water damage call.
risk: basement flooding, sewer backups and frozen pipes
risk_short: basement floods, sewer backups, frozen pipes
why: About 90% of Detroit homes were built before 1980, and most have basements. The city's sewers carry rain and sewage in the same pipes. In a heavy storm, the system fills and water backs up through basement floor drains. On June 25 and 26, 2021, several inches of rain fell in a few hours. Freeways flooded and tens of thousands of basements filled across the area.

It was not the first time. In August 2014, a similar storm flooded basements and highways across metro Detroit. Many older homes also have clay or cast-iron sewer lines that crack with age and roots. Winters are long and cold, and pipes in outside walls and vacant rooms freeze and split. Vacant homes nearby can hide leaks that spread to neighboring walls.
image_alt: Aerial view of cars on a flooded city street
image_caption: In June 2021, heavy rain flooded Detroit streets and freeways and filled basements.
problems: Older homes citywide in heavy rain
tips: Install a backwater valve on the basement floor drain.
Add sewer backup coverage to your policy; it is usually extra.
Store valuables off the basement floor on shelves.
Insulate pipes on outside walls before winter.
areas: Calls come from Corktown, Midtown, Jefferson-Chalmers, Indian Village, Boston-Edison, Grandmont Rosedale, Bagley and Woodbridge, plus Dearborn, Hamtramck and Southfield.

faq.q: Why does my Detroit basement flood in heavy rain?
faq.a: Detroit's sewers carry rain and sewage together. A big storm can fill them, and water backs up through the lowest drain in your home. A backwater valve stops most of that. Sewer backup coverage is usually extra on a home policy, so add it before the next storm.
